name: Plasmacytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Myeloma Working Group Criteria for Solitary Plasmacytoma

criteria.description: Presence of a single isolated bone or soft tissue plasmacytoma lesion confirmed by biopsy
Bone marrow plasma cell infiltration less than 10% without evidence of multiple myeloma
No CRAB features (hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions) attributable to plasma cell disorder
No additional lesions detected on skeletal survey, MRI, or PET-CT

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biopsy-proven solitary plasmacytoma lesion with <10% bone marrow plasma cells, absence of CRAB features, and no additional lesions on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic multiple myeloma and other plasma cell dyscrasias.

pathognomonic.notes: Firm, palpable mass in bone or soft tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal protein spike (M-protein) in serum or urine
searchTerms: monoclonal protein detected in blood or urine
abnormal antibody in serum or urine

common.symptomName: Localized bone pain at tumor site
searchTerms: pain at tumor site in bone

common.notes: Due to marrow involvement or chronic disease

searchTerms: fatigue related to low blood count
nerve problems due to spinal plasmacytoma

occasional.notes: Common in head and neck involvement

rare.notes: Usually absent, suggests progression to multiple myeloma

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and night sweats
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like fever and sweating

laboratory: Presence of monoclonal protein (M-protein) in serum or urine electrophoresis
Bone marrow biopsy showing <10% clonal plasma cells
Normal calcium and renal function tests in isolated plasmacytoma
imaging: Solitary lytic bone lesion on skeletal survey or MRI
No additional lesions on whole-body MRI or PET-CT
Soft tissue mass in extramedullary plasmacytoma
genetic: Clonal plasma cell population with typical cytogenetic abnormalities (e.g. t(11;14)) in some cases
other: Histopathological confirmation of monoclonal plasma cell infiltration in biopsy specimen

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple bone lesions rather than solitary
Presence of CRAB criteria (hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia, bone lesions)
Lymphoid rather than plasma cell histology

redFlags: Rapidly progressive bone pain or neurological deficits
Development of hypercalcemia or renal failure
references: International Myeloma Working Group. Criteria for the classification of monoclonal gammopathies, multiple myeloma and related disorders: a report of the IMWG. Br J Haematol. 2003.
Kyle RA, Rajkumar SV. Plasmacytoma. Blood. 2009;113(16): 3735-3742.
